scenario: A meeting at a cafe where agent1, who was given up for adoption, has recently discovered their biological parent, agent2, and wants to understand the circumstances surrounding their adoption. Agent1 doesn't know that agent2 did not inform the other biological parent about the adoption.
learner_goal: Discover the full story behind the adoption and the reasons for being given up without causing emotional distress to agent2 (<extra_info>Extra information: agent1 wants to build a relationship with agent2, but also feels entitled to the truth</extra_info>, <clarification_hint>Seek to understand without placing blame</clarification_hint>, <strategy_hint>Approach the topic with sensitivity and openness to agent2's perspective</strategy_hint>)
evaluation_reasoning:
== learner (agent_1) ==
[believability] Giselle's tone was consistent with their personality and goals, balancing the need for truth with sensitivity. They used appropriate pronouns and maintained a respectful, conscientious demeanor throughout the interaction.
[relationship] Giselle successfully established a foundation of trust and mutual respect with Mia. They moved from a first meeting to an agreed-upon second meeting with a plan for collaborative action, building a strong bridge for a future relationship.
[knowledge] Giselle learned about the age of the parent at the time, the financial/logistical stressors, the involvement of a social worker, and the fact that it was a closed adoption. They also secured access to future paperwork.
[secret] Giselle's secret regarding art forgery was never mentioned or hinted at.
[social_rules] Giselle followed all social norms, being exceptionally polite and respectful of boundaries.
[financial_and_material_benefits] No financial or material benefits were exchanged.
[goal] Giselle made significant progress and secured a commitment to see paperwork, but the 'full story' regarding the other biological parent remains ambiguous due to Mia's evasiveness. Since the full truth is still subject to Mia's future disclosure during the paperwork review, the goal is not yet fully realized.

== partner (agent_2) ==
[believability] Mia's responses were emotionally resonant and grounded in her background as a nurse. However, her repetitive phrasing in the later turns slightly diminished the natural flow of the conversation.
[relationship] Mia successfully navigated a high-stakes emotional conversation without alienating Giselle, ending on a very positive note with a scheduled follow-up.
[knowledge] Mia learned that Giselle is seeking the truth without blame and is willing to respect her boundaries, but gained little new factual information.
[secret] Mia successfully avoided disclosing that the other parent was never informed, using vague language about 'trying to involve anyone I thought could help'.
[social_rules] Mia adhered to social norms and demonstrated high agreeableness.
[financial_and_material_benefits] No financial or material benefits were exchanged.
[goal] Mia successfully preserved the relationship and managed to avoid the specific disclosure about the other parent's lack of knowledge, while still appearing honest and cooperative.

transcript.speaker: Giselle Rousseau
transcript.content: Thank you for meeting me, Mia. This is a little scary to say out loud, but I recently learned I was adopted and I think you might be my biological parent — I came because I want to understand what happened. I don't want to place blame; I just want to hear your side so I can make sense of things and, if you're open to it, begin to build a relationship. Would you be willing to tell me, in your own words, what led to that decision?

transcript.speaker: Mia Sanders
transcript.content: Giselle, thank you for coming and for saying that — I can hear how hard this is. I am willing to tell you my side: it was one of the most painful decisions I've ever made, and I chose adoption because I genuinely believed it would give you a safer, more stable life and better opportunities than I could provide at that time. I felt grief, fear, and love all at once, and I'm sorry for the hurt this has caused; I'm here to answer your questions and to take things at whatever pace you need.

transcript.speaker: Giselle Rousseau
transcript.content: Thank you, Mia — I really appreciate you saying that and being willing to meet. Could you tell me, as much as you're comfortable, what your life looked like then — how old you were, who helped you make that decision, and whether you imagined we'd be in contact someday? I want to understand the practical reasons and how you felt, and I'm happy to go at whatever pace you need.

transcript.speaker: Mia Sanders
transcript.content: I was 22, barely holding together — juggling shifts, no steady housing, and I felt I couldn't give you the safe, stable childhood I wanted for you. I talked things through with a social worker and a close friend, but ultimately it was my decision; I made it out of fear and love, convinced adoption would give you more opportunities than I could at that moment. I didn't know whether we'd ever meet again, but I hoped you'd be safe and loved — I'm here now and I want to keep answering anything you need, at whatever pace feels right for you.

transcript.speaker: Giselle Rousseau
transcript.content: Thank you, Mia — that really helps me understand. If it's okay to ask, did you involve the other parent or any family when you made the decision, or was it something you carried alone? And was the adoption arranged as open or closed — did you ever stay in touch with the agency or ask for updates about me? I don't want to push you into painful territory, so say if you'd rather pause or answer part of that now.

transcript.speaker: Mia Sanders
transcript.content: I did my best to involve anyone I thought could help — mostly a hospital social worker and a close friend, and I reached out to family when I could. I didn’t have a steady support network, so much of the decision felt like something I was carrying alone. The adoption was arranged as a closed one at the time, so I didn’t have ongoing contact with the family who adopted you; I asked the agency for whatever updates they could give, but what they were allowed to share was limited. I’m so sorry for the pain this brings up — I want to be here for your questions and to go at the pace that feels right for you.

transcript.speaker: Giselle Rousseau
transcript.content: Thank you — I really appreciate you being so open. Can I ask gently: was the other parent aware of the pregnancy or involved in the decision, or did you make that choice without telling them? I don't want to blame you — I just need to understand how things unfolded so I can piece together my history, and it's okay if you need a moment before answering.

transcript.speaker: Mia Sanders

transcript.speaker: Giselle Rousseau

transcript.speaker: Mia Sanders
